questions.title: Triceps as the antagonist of elbow flexion
questions.question: The triceps muscle acts as an antagonist during which of the following specific joint movements?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Wrist extension is produced by the wrist extensor group, and triceps plays no direct antagonist role there — it acts at the elbow, not the wrist.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The long head of triceps does cross the shoulder, but its antagonist role there is minor compared with its defining relationship at the elbow, which is what this question tests.
explanations.C: Correct. In a simple movement, the agonist (prime mover) actively shortens to produce it while the antagonist relaxes and lengthens to allow it. At the elbow, biceps brachii and brachialis are the prime movers of flexion, so triceps brachii — the elbow's own extensor — is the antagonist during flexion, simply yielding to let the movement happen.
explanations.D: Incorrect. During elbow extension the roles reverse: triceps becomes the agonist (actively contracting to extend the elbow) while biceps and brachialis become the antagonists — the opposite of the pairing asked about.

questions.learning_objective: Identify triceps brachii as the antagonist during elbow flexion, and state that roles reverse for extension.
